current_chain_id.meaning: current block.chainid of the executing (forked) chain

cached_chain_id.meaning: chain ID embedded in the EIP-712 DOMAIN_SEPARATOR stored immutably at deployment

validated_chain_id.meaning: chain ID in the domain separator the contract uses during signature verification

signature_from_current_chain.meaning: the off-chain intent signature was generated for the current (new) chain

signature_valid.meaning: EIP-712 signature verification succeeds in the contract

intent_flow_enabled.meaning: signature-based flows depositToIntent / depositToIntentWithPermit can proceed

preconditions.text: The DOMAIN_SEPARATOR is built once at deployment from the then-current block.chainid and stored immutably, and after a fork the live chain ID differs from the cached one (current_chain_id != cached_chain_id).
preconditions.derivation: separator_computed_with_chainid fixes cached_chain_id at the deployment chain ID; chain_id_changed makes the live chain ID differ from it after the fork.

safety.text: After a fork or chain ID change, the contract should validate against the current chain ID and accept an intent signature generated on the new chain.
safety.derivation: validate_against_current_chainid requires validation against the current chain ID so new-chain signatures are accepted.

effects.text: A signature generated on the new chain fails verification (signature_valid = false) and the signature-based flows depositToIntent / depositToIntentWithPermit cannot proceed (intent_flow_enabled = false).
effects.derivation: signatures_invalid_on_new_chain: new-chain signature does not match the cached separator; flows_dos: signature-based flows are broken, denying intent verification.

effect_coverage.reason: models one new-chain signature failing verification; the aggregate 'all off-chain signatures' is not expressible without quantifiers.
models the flows as disabled; the asserted permanence of the denial-of-service is temporal and not expressible.

assumptions: The contract verifies intent signatures against its stored DOMAIN_SEPARATOR and does not recompute it after deployment.
The fork / chain ID change occurs after deployment and the contract is not redeployed.
Off-chain signers build the EIP-712 domain using the chain ID of the chain they intend to transact on.
unresolved: No attacker or trigger for the fork / chain ID change is identified; the scenario is hypothetical.
Report does not state whether signatures generated before the fork remain valid on the new chain.
No update or recovery mechanism for the cached DOMAIN_SEPARATOR is mentioned.

limitations: Aggregate claim 'all off-chain signatures become invalid' is not formalized (no quantifiers); only a single new-chain signature is modeled.
Permanence of the DoS is asserted only for the forked chain; persistent and temporal claims are out of scope.
Population-wide and economic impacts of broken intent flows are not formalized.
The causal mechanism linking the cached separator to the verification result (root_cause / action statements) is not a permitted P source, so preconditions assert only the chain-ID mismatch.
